Immersion instructions

01

Settle into the chair.

Your body rests in the chair. A simulated lifetime unfolds around you. Choose your language and reading settings before entering.

02

Choose your starting conditions.

Random is the default. You may choose a body profile, an upbringing range and a ten-point starting shape.

01
03

Read the turns.

Follow health, wellbeing and money. Event markers explain changes; they do not predict your future.

04

Look back.

Return to your record. See the decisions, people and events that shaped this life, then try another path.

Time controls

Ⅱ　2×　3×　10×　20×

Pause to look. Use 2×, 3×, 10× or 20× to move faster.

Plan for 70–80 simulated years. A life may end earlier. Choices begin at 10.

Research

What is measured?

This prototype uses authored game rules. Its money, health changes and event odds are not measured population statistics.

The graphs join five-year snapshots. Markers sit at the recorded review age, not an exact event date.

Ten points are a game constraint. Reasoning, empathy and strength are not biological opposites.

The neighbourhood is metaphorical. Nearby buildings represent parts of a life, not a real map.

Marriage and family milestones follow your choices. Dengue, job loss and pregnancy are not yet generated by this model.

Body, mind and experience

Inherited differences and environments interact. Heritability describes population variation, not an unchangeable percentage of a person.

Big Five traits, reasoning, emotional skills and empathy are distinct. Personality can change. No trait prohibits a career.

These game indices are not psychological tests or dopamine measurements. Comparisons use modeled paths, not a real population average.

The world behind the chair

The chair-service premise draws on the author's Two Layers and The Convenience. This software does not claim to provide physical immersion or medical treatment.

Universe 25 was an enclosed-mouse experiment, not proof that human prosperity causes extinction.
